EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN  
“Clean Air Act Amendments, Non-Attainment Status, and Manufacturing Activity, 1968-1982”

-------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
-------------------------------------------------
Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with a dynamic event-study extension and staggered treatment timing (Sun & Abraham 2021 / Callaway & Sant’Anna 2021).

Why appropriate  
• Exogenous policy shock: non-attainment designations were triggered by measured ambient pollution levels relative to federally set standards, not by local economic conditions per se.  
• Rich panel: plant-level outcomes observed before and after designation for treated and never-treated counties.  
• Staggered timing: first wave of designations after the 1970 CAAA (effectively 1972) and a second wave after the 1977 Amendments (1978-79). Modern staggered-timing DID estimators handle different adoption cohorts.  
• Plant fixed effects absorb time-invariant plant characteristics; year-by-state or year-by-region fixed effects absorb common shocks.

-------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
-------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
Treated = 1 if plant i is located in county c that is designated “non-attainment” for the primary National Ambient Air Quality Standard (NAAQS) for total suspended particulates (TSP) or ozone beginning in year τc; 0 otherwise.

Treatment timing / event date  
τc = first calendar year in which county c appears on the EPA non-attainment list:  
• 1972–73 (post-1970 CAAA)  
• 1978–79 (post-1977 CAAA)  
The treatment indicator switches on permanently from τc forward (sharp adoption).

Control group  
Plants in counties that remain “attainment” throughout 1968-1982 serve as controls. As robustness we will restrict controls to counties in the same state (or air-quality control region) that were always in attainment to improve comparability.

Unit of analysis: plant-year.

-------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
-------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends: In the absence of designation, outcome trends for plants in (future) non-attainment and always-attainment counties would have evolved similarly.  
• Plausibility: same macro shocks, common industry trends; can be inspected with pre-treatment event-study coefficients.

A2. No anticipation: Plants did not change behavior before public release of the non-attainment list.  
• Plausibility: The 1970 Act signaled eventual regulation but county-level assignments were not known until monitoring data were evaluated; still test by including leads.

A3. Stable unit treatment value / no spillovers: Regulations in county c do not directly affect plants in attainment counties.  
• Plausibility: Some cross-county pollution transport exists; border robustness will test for spillovers.

A4. Composition stability: Entry/exit decisions are not differentially changing in anticipation in a way that violates SUTVA. We will address by keeping a balanced panel and examining exit rates.

-------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation
-------------------------------------------------
T1. Endogenous designation (reverse causality)  
• Counties with heavy industrial activity produced more pollution and therefore were more likely to be classified non-attainment, biasing estimates downward.  
Mitigation:  
  – Include county fixed effects (absorbs level differences).  
  – Event-study pre-trends; if parallel, endogeneity is less worrying.  
  – Instrumental-variables robustness: instrument designation with up-wind monitor readings or topographic inversion frequency.

T2. Differential local shocks (e.g., energy crises, recessions)  
• If shocks hit treated and control counties differently in the post-period, DID may capture these shocks.  
Mitigation:  
  – Add state-year or region-industry-year fixed effects.  
  – Control for county-specific linear trends.  
  – Placebo checks on pre-period shocks (1965 Clean Air Act minor amendments).

T3. Plant relocation / spillovers  
• Firms may move plants from non-attainment to nearby attainment counties, depressing outcomes in treated counties and inflating them in controls.  
Mitigation:  
  – Compare treated counties to attainment counties that are >50 miles away (exclude border counties).  
  – Track plant IDs to detect cross-county moves; re-estimate excluding movers.

-------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
-------------------------------------------------
```r
#--- 0. Packages -------------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)      # fast data wrangling
library(fixest)          # fast fixed-effect regressions incl. Sun & Abraham
library(did)             # Callaway & Sant'Anna staggered DID
library(ggplot2)         # plotting event study

#--- 1. Load data ------------------------------------------------------------
plants <- fread("plants_data.csv")   # ensure plant_id, county_fips, year, output, employment, na_status, first_na_year

#--- 2. Construct variables --------------------------------------------------
plants[, treat := as.integer(year >= first_na_year & na_status == 1)]
plants[, event_time := year - first_na_year]    # event-study relative year
plants[, post := as.integer(event_time >= 0 & na_status == 1)]

# Log outcomes
plants[, ln_output := log(output)]
plants[, ln_employ := log(employment)]

# Keep balanced panel 1968-1982 (optional robustness)
balanced <- plants[, .N, by = plant_id][N==length(1968:1982)]$plant_id
plants_bal <- plants[plant_id %in% balanced]

#--- 3. Main DID regression --------------------------------------------------
# Sun & Abraham estimator (feols with sunab())
did_sa <- feols(ln_output ~ sunab(first_na_year, year) | plant_id + state_year,
                data = plants,
                cluster = ~county_fips)
summary(did_sa)

#--- 4. Plot dynamic effects -------------------------------------------------
iplot(did_sa, ref.line = 0, xlab = "Years relative to first designation",
      ylab = "Log output effect")

#--- 5. Robustness: county-specific trends -----------------------------------
did_trend <- feols(ln_output ~ sunab(first_na_year, year) | plant_id + state_year + county_fips[year],
                   data = plants,
                   cluster = ~county_fips)
summary(did_trend)

#--- 6. Alternative outcome: employment --------------------------------------
did_emp <- feols(ln_employ ~ sunab(first_na_year, year) | plant_id + state_year,
                 data = plants,
                 cluster = ~county_fips)
summary(did_emp)

#--- 7. Callaway & Sant'Anna estimator --------------------------------------
cs <- att_gt(yname = "ln_output",
             tname = "year",
             idname = "plant_id",
             gname = "first_na_year",
             xformla = ~1,
             data = plants)
agg_effects <- aggte(cs, type = "dynamic")
summary(agg_effects)
```

Notes  
• state_year is an interaction FE constructed as paste0(state_fips,"_",year).  
• county_fips[year] syntax in `feols` adds county-specific linear trends.  
• Clustered SEs at county level.

-------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
-------------------------------------------------
Prior: Stricter air-quality regulation raises compliance costs, especially energy-intensive, pollution-intensive production. I expect:  
• Output: −3 % to −6 % within five years after designation.  
• Employment: slightly smaller decline, −2 % to −4 %.  
Over time, effects may attenuate as firms adopt abatement technology.

-------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)  
(C1–C5 adapted from Angrist & Pischke, 2014)

C1: Parallel pre-trends visually and statistically verified ………… 0.8  
C2: No anticipation / clean pre-period leads ………………………… 0.7  
C3: No spillovers or interference ……………………………………… 0.6  
C4: Stable treatment definition (no contamination) ………………… 0.8  
C5: Correct timing and functional form (staggered DID with SA) … 0.9  

Average score ≈ 0.76 → reasonably credible, with main residual concern being potential spillovers and endogenous designation.

-------------------------------------------------
End of Plan
